text:
maya: heads-up — saw a 12-18% p50 latency bump on canary for mixtral-8x at ~18:12 UTC. Only on chat-template workloads where prompts include the new assistant/system delim.

owen: ugh. is this the kv-cache warmup thrash we saw before or something new? any kernel fallbacks in the logs?

maya: logs attached below (snippet). Kernel picker flipped to byte-fallback path around token 30 of convo for many requests. Looks correlated with prompts that include trailing "\n---\n" chat separators.

```
2026-03-17T18:12:03Z [req=abcd] model=mixtral-8x kernel=optimized_rope kernel_switch=byte_fallback reason=tokenizer_byte_fallback token_idx=30
2026-03-17T18:12:03Z [req=abcd] kv_prefetch: evicted=0 prefetched=2 cache_hits=0
2026-03-17T18:12:03Z [req=abcd] latency_token_ms=12.4 total_ms=210
```

jia: interesting. sounds like the tokenizer is generating a byte-fallback token mid-sequence (likely a special delimiter or system prompt chunk). byte_fallback triggers different kernel which doesn't use kv-prefetch the same way — yields lower throughput and higher per-token latency.

carol: can you paste an example prompt that reproduces? my guess: the new chat template injects invisible unicode or CRLF sequence that trips the byte tokenizer.

maya: repro prompt (sanitized):
```
[System]
You are a helpful assistant.
---
[User]
Give me a summary of the docs.
```

owen: that "---" is ASCII but if the client adds zero-width joiner or non-breaking space around separators we hit byte fallback. Also note: mixtral kernel chooser currently uses `rope_scale` inference heuristic + naive token-encoding predictor. If the predictor misestimates byte vs rope tokens we can prefer a kernel that ultimately switches mid-stream.

jia: two immediate mitigations to try: 1) increase `kv_prefetch_count` from 2 -> 4 for mixtral-8x canary so prefetch covers swapped kernels; 2) add a short-circuit to re-evaluate tokenizer output early in the request so kernel picker doesn't change after token 0 (i.e., lock kernel on first non-empty token). Both low-risk.

carol: second option sounds safer long-term. locking kernel on first token avoids mid-stream kernel swap but we need to ensure memory usage for pessimistic kernel is acceptable. what's the worst-case memory delta?

owen: for mixtral-8x optimistic kernel -> byte fallback memory delta ~200MB on our instance types. We can cap by using `rope_scale_override` to align RoPE up to 1.02 for models with known scale issues; that reduces misalignment and avoids fallback in many cases.

maya: ran a quick profile with `perf` and the runtime trace. attaching small flame output. Key call stacks: kernel_selector::evaluate -> tokenizer_probe -> kernel_switch -> kv_cache::warmup. The spike happens during kernel_switch when tokenizer_probe returns `BYTE_FALLBACK`.

```
# simplified perf sample
  45% kernel_switch
  20% kv_cache::warmup
  15% memcpy
  10% tokenizer_probe
  10% other
```

jia: for model-specific tuning we should add a table: {model -> tokenizer_probe_thresholds, rope_scale_override, default_kv_prefetch}. I'll create a PR with entries for llama-2-13b, mistral-7b-instruct, mixtral-8x, qwen-7b. For mixtral-8x set `tokenizer_probe_threshold=64` and `rope_scale_override=1.01` as a starting point.

carol: are we sure `tokenizer_probe_threshold` shouldn't be lower? if it's too high we might lock to a wrong kernel early.

owen: probed tokens should be heuristically chosen: use first 2 tokens plus lookahead of special-token detection. Implementation: run tokenizer.encode on first N bytes until we hit whitespace or special delimiter or N==16. That will cover most chat separators.

maya: regarding batching heuristics: current batch coalescer waits up to `batch_timeout_ms=8` for mixtral canary; with kernel switching we see jitter. Suggested change: dynamic timeout that increases to 12ms when a request's tokenizer_probe indicates probable byte-encoded tokens so coalescer can batch more similar kernel requests together.

jia: good call — we can also tag requests with `kernel_hint` from tokenizer_probe so coalescer groups by hint. That avoids mixing different kernel types in a batch.

infra-bot: deploy queued: canary/mixtral-8x kernel-locker v2026.03.17-1 -> scheduled 2026-03-17T19:00:00Z by jia.

maya: quick canary notes after rolling to 10% at 19:10: p50 back to baseline, p99 slightly improved. no sign of excessive memory pressure.

carol: nice. follow-ups?

owen: 1) telemetry: emit `tokenizer_probe_result` tag in traces for 7 days. 2) PR to add model tuning table. 3) longer-term: make kernel selector consider `rope_scale` and `head_dim` at selection time (not just runtime fallback).

jia: filing tasks: ENG-RUNTIME-441 (telemetry), ENG-RUNTIME-442 (tuning table PR), ENG-RUNTIME-443 (batcher grouping by kernel_hint).

maya: thanks all — saved the canary screenshots to the #perf-dash link. :thumbsup:

owen: :raised_hands: closing the investigation for now. reopen if we see recurrence.
